persistence_invariants.brief: The up migration (add batch_number/serial_number, backfill, drop inventory_code) runs as a single atomic unit: every pre-existing row survives with unchanged identity and canonical location, row count is preserved, or the whole migration rolls back (R1, AC3).

batch_number and serial_number are NULLABLE so a non-conforming inventory_code backfills to NULL rather than a guessed value or a dropped row; the migration must tolerate short/malformed codes without raising (AC2).

The Alembic migration is reversible: downgrade re-adds inventory_code and reconstructs it from canonical location + batch_number + serial_number, dropping the new columns and restoring the pre-migration schema shape; a full up-then-down round trip is clean (AC6).

The UNIQUE(sku, location) composite key is untouched by the refactor: location stays canonical and no new column replaces it, so every (sku, location) pair remains uniquely addressable across the migration (R3).

nfrs.brief: This is a purely-additive-then-destructive migration over an EXISTING stock table, so its guarantee is genuine row survival (unlike F1's create-table migration): every stock record present before the migration exists after it with the same identity and unchanged canonical location; row count is preserved and no row is lost or corrupted. Realized by an atomic Alembic migration (PI1) and verified by a real-branch round-trip test (R4).

N/A for this feature — the split-tracking refactor changes only the stock record's schema and display, not quantity math or the write path. The no-overcommit / non-negative guarantee (CHECK + service guard) established in F1 is preserved unchanged; this feature introduces no code that could drive quantity negative.

Every (sku, location) pair remains uniquely addressable across the migration. Location stays canonical and is NOT recreated from inventory_code, so the UNIQUE(sku, location) constraint (PI4) is untouched; the migration must not drop or alter it. Verified against the real branch (R4).

Every AC in this feature is verified by integration tests running against the paired Lakebase branch (databricks_postgres via DATABASE_URL), never a mock or in-memory substitute; migrations are applied to the branch first. CI refuses a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch.

The boundary stays a JSON API returning data (not server-rendered HTML); the React + TypeScript SPA under client/ renders batch_number and serial_number as separate fields with client-side navigation and in-place updates. Realized in S2 (API) and S3 (UI); the API paths are covered by the R4 branch integration tests and the UI by client component tests.

The migration surfaces the count of non-conforming rows (those left with NULL batch_number/serial_number) before the change is accepted, so an operator can review the blast radius against the acceptable-threshold open question. Owned by the migration/operational tooling as a COUNT probe emitted to the migration log, never as domain logic. Verified on the real branch (R4, AC4).

The migration adds and backfills the new columns before dropping inventory_code, and the drop runs only after integrity is verified (AC4 -> AC5 ordering), so the destructive step is gated on a clean probe. This honors the PO preference for additive-where-possible migrations and gives the reversibility path (AC6) a clean rollback point.

A stock row whose batch_number/serial_number are NULL (non-conforming legacy code) renders cleanly in the SPA: batch and serial default to an explicit 'not tracked' indication, never a null crash or a blank region. Owned by the client presentation layer over the JSON boundary; covered by a SPA component test on the untracked path plus the R4 branch integration test. (PO preference.)
